title: Agriculture types
examples: What is the main difference between growing food for yourself and growing food to sell?
When did the Green Revolution happen and what did it involve?
Can you give me an example of a cash crop grown in commercial farming?

explain.say: Today we are learning about different types of farming.
Subsistence farming is when farmers grow food just to feed their own families.
Commercial farming focuses on producing large amounts of goods for sale.
The Green Revolution was a major scientific change in farming.
A real-life example is comparing a small village garden to a huge wheat farm.

draw.text: Real Life: Garden vs. Wheat Farm

explain.say: A common mistake is thinking all large farms are commercial.

items: Some large farms might still feed local people.
Size does not always mean the goal is profit.

draw.text: Mistake: All big farms sell goods

faq.q: What is the main difference between subsistence and commercial farming?
faq.a: Subsistence farming is mainly for feeding the local family, while commercial farming is done to sell goods for profit.
asks: How do I tell if a farm is subsistence or commercial?
What is the main goal of each farming type?

faq.q: What was the Green Revolution really about?
faq.a: It was a period of major scientific advancements that increased crop yields significantly using new technologies.
asks: Did the Green Revolution just mean more tractors?
What scientific changes boosted food supply?

faq.q: Are cash crops always grown in commercial settings?
faq.a: Yes, cash crops are grown specifically to be sold in a market, which is typical of commercial farming.
asks: If I grow bananas to sell, is that commercial?
What is the purpose of growing a cash crop?

faq.q: Does technology level determine the farming type?
faq.a: Not necessarily; while commercial farming uses high technology, some subsistence farms can still use modern tools.
asks: Must I use big machines to be commercial?
Can technology be used in small farming?

faq.a: A cash crop is any crop grown specifically to be sold for money, rather than for direct consumption.
asks: Give me an example of a cash crop.
Why do farmers grow crops to sell?

facts: Subsistence farming relies heavily on traditional knowledge and local resources.
Commercial farming often involves monoculture, growing only one crop type.
The Green Revolution introduced high-yield varieties of staple crops.
Cash crops are grown primarily for export or sale in larger markets.

quiz.say: A farmer grows yams and beans only to feed his village.
quiz.why: This activity shows the goal is feeding the family, not making money.

wrong.0: Cash cropping means the crop is meant to be sold, which is not the goal here.
wrong.2: This implies selling the goods for profit, which is not the case here.
wrong.3: This refers to a time period of scientific change, not a farming method itself.

quiz.say: Growing maize for export to another country is an example of:
quiz.why: Exporting goods means the primary goal is making money in a market.

wrong.1: This type focuses only on feeding the local community.
wrong.2: This is a historical event, not the name for the farming system.
wrong.3: This term is too vague; commercial farming describes the market goal better.

quiz.say: The use of genetically modified seeds to increase yield is linked to:
quiz.why: The Green Revolution was marked by scientific inputs like new seeds and fertilizers.

wrong.0: This describes the goal of subsistence, not the technology used to achieve high yields.
wrong.2: This method relies on older, local seed varieties.
wrong.3: While commercial farms use these, the term describes the scientific breakthrough.
